name: releasing
conclusion_quantitative: releasing (Escalate) specifies 3 of 5 categories: 4 autonomy limits, 4 approval gates, 10+ validation rules; none for clarification rules, escalation rules. Strongest: validation rules.
conclusion_qualitative: releasing runs the dde release process: choose the version, write the changelog entry, make a signed commit and signed tag, push after approval, then update the GitHub release. Pushing is never automatic because it triggers a public release workflow; the user confirms the version and the push. Signatures and the release page are verified against a checklist. It sets no clarification rules or rules for escalating failures.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 4 autonomy limits (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly prose.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly running text. The agent never pushes automatically, never edits the version placeholder by hand, always signs and signs off commits without skipping hooks, and never rewrites a published tag.

statements.quote: Always a new commit; never rewrite a published tag.

clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to ask the user for missing or unclear information, or to avoid guessing.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 4 approval gates (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly prose.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly running text. The user confirms the target version before anything is written, and because the tag triggers a costly public release the agent never pushes on its own but asks and waits for explicit confirmation.

statements.quote: **Ask the user to confirm** the target version before writing anything
The release workflow is expensive and public; always confirm.

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ validation rules (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The agent checks the commit and tag signatures and the published release page, and runs a checklist: confirmed version, user-visible changelog only, correct date, placeholder untouched, signed commit and tag, no push without approval and release notes filled.

statements.quote: Commit signature must show `Good signature`; tag must start with `tag v<new-version>` and carry a PGP block.
CHANGELOG entry lists only user-visible changes
`src/Application.php` NOT modified (placeholder is injected by CI)
Commit signed + signed-off, subject `chore(release): document v<version>`
No push without explicit user approval
GitHub release notes populated from CHANGELOG section

escalation.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent what to do when something goes wrong, such as stopping or reporting an error to the user.
